t.5.27.1: Auspicious omens came to her, the blameless and lovely one, who was in such a state, distressed, bereft of joy and wretched at heart, just as dependents flock to a man favoured by fortune.
t.5.27.2: The auspicious left eye of that lady with beautiful hair, with its curved lashes, framed by a fringe of lashes, dark of pupil and wide in its white, began to throb by itself, like a reddish lotus struck by a fish.
t.5.27.4: And her thigh, plump and well-formed like the trunk of a lordly elephant, one of the pair pressed close together, throbbing again, proclaimed that Rāma stood before her.
t.5.27.3: And her left arm, lovely, curved, plump and round, worthy of the costliest black aloe and sandal paste, long pillowed by her peerless beloved, suddenly trembled.
t.5.27.5: Then the lovely garment, golden in hue and seemingly a little soiled with dust, slipped down slightly from the clear-eyed, graceful-limbed lady with finely pointed teeth as she stood there.
t.5.27.6: Roused by these and other omens, long since proven true and auspicious, the fair-browed lady rejoiced once more, like a seed withered by wind and heat and all but lost that revives with the rain.
t.5.27.7: Her face, with lips like the bimba fruit, lovely eyes, brows and hairline, curving lashes and gleaming white teeth, shone once more, like the moon set free from the mouth of Rāhu.
t.5.27.8: Her grief gone, her weariness dispelled, her fever calmed and her spirit awakened by joy, that noble lady shone with her face as a night in the bright fortnight shines with the risen cool-rayed moon.
